AccessEvent.description: One entry of a tenant's access audit trail.
AccessEvent.title: AccessEvent

Activation.description: The result of checking a schedule before it is switched on.
Activation.title: Activation

AdoptCheck.description: What one item would become in knowledge.
AdoptCheck.title: AdoptCheck

AgentConfig.description:
Everything about one agent node; mirrors the arguments of ``orkexa.Agent``.

``model`` names the provider and the model (``provider:model``). ``thinking``,
``thinking_display``, ``thinking_budget``, ``cache_control``, ``cache_ttl``, ``fallbacks`` and
``server_tools`` depend on what the model supports (:mod:`nodestro_runtime.model_profile`); a model that
cannot use one refuses a value other than its default (see :mod:`nodestro_runtime.agent_builder`).

``max_tokens`` is the most output tokens per model response (reasoning counts against it); it may not exceed
the model's documented or declared maximum (``GET /api/models/profile``). The upper bound here only catches
typos: no model accepts more.
AgentConfig.title: AgentConfig

AgentDraft.description: What the editor shows after "Describe agent".
AgentDraft.title: AgentDraft

AgentModel.description: The model one agent of a template gets, and why.
AgentModel.title: AgentModel

AgentTestResult.description: Everything the inspector shows after a test; never stored as a workflow run.
AgentTestResult.title: AgentTestResult

ApiCheck.description: Whether a saved workflow version can be published, and what to know about it.
ApiCheck.title: ApiCheck

ApiKeyOut.description: A key as the studio shows it: everything but the hash.
ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut

ApiLimits.description: How much a published API may be used; exceeded limits answer ``429``.
ApiLimits.title: ApiLimits

ApprovalConfig.description: A pause for a person who approves or rejects the results that arrive here.
ApprovalConfig.title: ApprovalConfig

ApprovalOut.description: An approval that waits for a decision: what to review and how to answer.
ApprovalOut.title: ApprovalOut

ApprovalRecord.description: A person's decision at an approval node; nothing is ever approved automatically.
ApprovalRecord.title: ApprovalRecord

ArchitectReasoning.description:
The reasoning of one request of a job: ``step`` is ``analysis``, ``plan``, ``agent_revision`` or ``repair``,
or for the sub-requests ``agent`` (the Agent Architect designs an agent) and ``tool`` (the Coding Agent writes a
tool), whose ``subject`` names the agent or tool (RT-063).
ArchitectReasoning.title: ArchitectReasoning

ArchiveEntry.description: One entry of a ZIP archive.
ArchiveEntry.title: ArchiveEntry

BackupInfo.description: What the user confirms before a restore.
BackupInfo.title: BackupInfo

BatchPlan.description: What a batch would do; nothing starts.
BatchPlan.title: BatchPlan

BatchRow.description: One input: form values and/or free text.
BatchRow.title: BatchRow

BlockedRequest.description: A model request that waits: the one that was refused, and the ones held while the decision is pending.
BlockedRequest.title: BlockedRequest

BudgetBlock.description: The limit that refused the request.
BudgetBlock.title: BudgetBlock

BudgetRaise.description: One approved raise of a run's budget (BUDGET-1); the request in ``budget_requests`` holds the full record.
BudgetRaise.title: BudgetRaise

BudgetRequest.description: A budget decision of one top-level run: what blocked, the numbers when it was asked, and the decision.
BudgetRequest.title: BudgetRequest

BuildInput.description: One pinned upstream file a catalog model is built from (what an offline build needs on this computer).
BuildInput.title: BuildInput

BuiltinSandboxStatus.description: Whether the built-in Linux sandbox isolates AI-generated code on this computer (desktop profile only).
BuiltinSandboxStatus.title: BuiltinSandboxStatus

BuiltinToolInfo.description: A built-in tool's catalog entry (its spec) with the description the model reads.
BuiltinToolInfo.title: BuiltinToolInfo

CaseOrigin.description: Where a test case proposed from a run came from (Q-4).
CaseOrigin.title: CaseOrigin

CaseProposal.description: A test case proposed from a failed run; stored only when it is saved into a series.
CaseProposal.title: CaseProposal

ChatLimits.description: Limits of the live chat of one run (all its orchestrators together).
ChatLimits.title: ChatLimits

ChatTarget.description: An orchestrator node a person can talk to.
ChatTarget.title: ChatTarget

CheckIssue.description: A finding of the workflow check, attributed to a node or a connection where possible.
CheckIssue.title: CheckIssue

ConditionConfig.description: A deterministic decision on an earlier result; no AI request is made.
ConditionConfig.title: ConditionConfig

ConditionRule.description: One named branch of a decision node: taken when ``field`` compared with ``value`` holds.
ConditionRule.title: ConditionRule

ConfigIssue.description: A problem with an agent configuration; ``code``/``params`` are shown in the UI language.
ConfigIssue.title: ConfigIssue

ConnectionEvent.description: An administration event (who changed which connection); never secrets or settings values.
ConnectionEvent.title: ConnectionEvent

ConnectionIn.description: A new connection. The secret is set separately (:meth:`ConnectionService.set_secret`).
ConnectionIn.title: ConnectionIn

ConnectionPatch.description: A change of a connection; the type cannot change.
ConnectionPatch.title: ConnectionPatch

ConnectionView.description: What every read returns: the connection without its secret, with ``secret_set``.
ConnectionView.title: ConnectionView

ContextRef.description: One object a message was sent with: exactly the snapshot the model saw.
ContextRef.title: ContextRef

ContractField.description: A field of a team's output contract with its description in the language (its label for people).
ContractField.title: ContractField

ContractFieldSummary.description: One field of a workflow's output contract, as the workflow list shows it.
ContractFieldSummary.title: ContractFieldSummary

ConversationFile.description: A file attached to a conversation (an input file of origin ``assistant``).
ConversationFile.title: ConversationFile

CostEstimate.description: What a number of runs will probably cost, from earlier runs of the workflow.
CostEstimate.title: CostEstimate

DecisionNote.description: What the orchestrator decided in the step an instruction was part of (data of the record, no reasoning).
DecisionNote.title: DecisionNote

DecisionRecord.description: How a decision node decided: the value it saw and the branches it opened.
DecisionRecord.title: DecisionRecord

DependencyStatus.description: What the UI shows for a scope: what is needed, what is approved and installed.
DependencyStatus.title: DependencyStatus

EdgeLoop.description:
Makes a connection a loop: following it runs the nodes from its target to its source again.

A loop leaves a decision or approval node through one of its branches and leads back to a node
before it. ``max_iterations`` is mandatory and counts the first run; ``on_exhausted`` says what
happens when the branch is taken once more: ``fail`` ends the run as failed
(``run.loop_exhausted``), ``continue`` ignores the loop, so the node's other open branches decide.
EdgeLoop.title: EdgeLoop

EnvironmentInfo.description: An environment directory on disk, for the maintenance page.
EnvironmentInfo.title: EnvironmentInfo

ErrorCodeCatalog.description: Every problem code of the studio API and the runtime, sorted, with its parameters.
ErrorCodeCatalog.title: ErrorCodeCatalog

ErrorResponse.description: Every error of the studio API: ``code`` is stable (the interface translates it with ``params``), ``detail`` an English technical text. Validation errors (``request.invalid``) list ``params.errors`` (``loc``, ``msg``, ``type``; the input is never echoed).
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ExampleMessage.description: A message placed before the task, e.g. a few-shot example.
ExampleMessage.title: ExampleMessage

ExportJob.description: A portable export being built (kept in the database; a restart marks a running one as interrupted).
ExportJob.title: ExportJob

ExportedDefinition.description: The dependency part of an exported workflow: no approvals, they never travel.
ExportedDefinition.title: ExportedDefinition

FileRetention.description:
How long files attached in assistant conversations are kept (API-056), set by an administrator.

``None`` (the default) keeps them until the user removes them or deletes the conversation, as before. With a
number of days, every conversation file attached longer ago than that is removed by the input file clean-up
(``POST /api/inputs/cleanup``) and, in the desktop app, at start and then hourly; its conversation and messages
stay, and a sent message keeps only the file's name.
FileRetention.title: FileRetention

FileSupport.description: What the assistant accepts, and what its current model reads natively.
FileSupport.title: FileSupport

FileUpload.description: One uploaded file: attached (``file``) or refused (``problem``, nothing is stored then).
FileUpload.title: FileUpload

FileView.description: A conversation file with how the assistant's current model would receive it.
FileView.title: FileView

GateOverride.description: The written reason for releasing despite failed non-critical gate items.
GateOverride.title: GateOverride

GateRecord.description: What the gate said when a release was created, and the override if one was given.
GateRecord.title: GateRecord

GuidanceRef.description: One instruction of a person that was part of an orchestrator decision's prompt.
GuidanceRef.title: GuidanceRef

Guide.description: What the gallery and the documentation explain about one example.
Guide.title: Guide

Handover.description: A proposal to continue in an existing Nodestro function; the user decides there.
Handover.title: Handover

Hardware.description: What this computer offers to local models (memory sizes in bytes; ``None``: not known).
Hardware.title: Hardware

InputField.description: One field of a workflow's input form (see :mod:`nodestro_runtime.forms`).
InputField.title: InputField

InputFileOut.description: An input file for the interface (without the internal blob ids).
InputFileOut.title: InputFileOut

JobLayer.description: One file (layer) of a model download, as Ollama reports it.
JobLayer.title: JobLayer

JobStep.description: One step of a job, as the code runs it.
JobStep.title: JobStep

JudgeVerdict.description: The verdict of the AI judge; always shown as an AI judgement.
JudgeVerdict.title: JudgeVerdict

KnowledgeConfig.description:
Which knowledge files an agent gets and how.

``context`` puts the files into the prompt, ``on_demand`` gives the agent the
``files`` tool to load them when needed, ``search`` gives it the ``search``
tool over their text (RAG with citations).

``retrieval`` is how ``search`` ranks: ``default`` follows the workspace setting, ``fts`` full text,
``vector`` semantic search (needs the semantic index), ``hybrid`` both.
KnowledgeConfig.title: KnowledgeConfig

KnowledgeIndexStatus.description: The semantic index of the knowledge base: which model filled it and how complete it is.
KnowledgeIndexStatus.title: KnowledgeIndexStatus

KnowledgeProposal.description: Content an agent proposed for knowledge; stored there only after a person confirmed it.
KnowledgeProposal.title: KnowledgeProposal

KnowledgeProposalConfig.description: An agent may propose its result (and parts of it) for knowledge; a person always decides.
KnowledgeProposalConfig.title: KnowledgeProposalConfig

LegacyReport.description: What the activation step stamped (shown as *exceptions from before S-2*).
LegacyReport.title: LegacyReport

LiveAnswer.description: An answer being written in this process: what has arrived so far (shown live, never stored as such).
LiveAnswer.title: LiveAnswer

LocalAdvice.description:
A hint about the local models of this computer; the interface shows its own text for the ``code``.

``value`` and ``recommended`` depend on the code: tokens for ``local.context_small``, tokens per second times ten
for ``local.model_slow``, bytes for ``local.memory_low``.
LocalAdvice.title: LocalAdvice

LocalModelInfo.description: A local model of a release, as this installation knows it.
LocalModelInfo.title: LocalModelInfo

LocalStatus.description: The state of the local model server of this workspace.
LocalStatus.title: LocalStatus

McpServerHealth.description: What this process knows about one server since it started (no secrets, no arguments).
McpServerHealth.title: McpServerHealth

McpServerView.description: A server as the API shows it: without its token.
McpServerView.title: McpServerView

McpStats.description: Operational state for administrators (WP-7): calls in flight, the operator's limits, per-server health.
McpStats.title: McpStats

McpToolRef.description:
An MCP tool frozen in a release bundle (WP-9): the approved definition the release was published with.

It names the server by id and slug only: no address, no token, no credentials. A release run uses the tool only
while the tenant still has the same server with this tool approved at exactly this hash and classification
(``mcp.release_tool_changed`` otherwise). Defined here, not in :mod:`nodestro_runtime.mcp`, so a runtime copy
without the MCP client (an exported project) can still read bundles.
McpToolRef.title: McpToolRef

Measurement.description: One model's newest matching test run.
Measurement.title: Measurement

MemoryConfig.description: ``run`` keeps memory for one workflow run, ``persistent`` in a named space.
MemoryConfig.title: MemoryConfig

MemoryRef.description: A persistent memory space an agent reads and writes: live data shared by all runs.
MemoryRef.title: MemoryRef

explanation.description: Two sentences on what the agent will remember and why.
explanation.title: Explanation

files.description: Two to five small, well-organised memory files.
files.title: Files

ModelAlternative.description: A model that is ready now and can do what the action needs.
ModelAlternative.title: ModelAlternative

ModelCapabilities.description: What a model supports according to Orkexa, for a model id typed in the editor (not only catalog entries).
ModelCapabilities.title: ModelCapabilities

ModelPolicy.description: How a model is chosen from measurements; nothing in it is a quality value of its own.
ModelPolicy.title: ModelPolicy

ModelProblem.description: Why a local model cannot be used for an action now, and what may be done about it.
ModelProblem.title: ModelProblem

ModelProfile.description: Capabilities, limits and agent options of one model as the workspace runs it.
ModelProfile.title: ModelProfile

ModelSpeed.description: How fast an installed model answered here, measured by :meth:`LocalModelService.benchmark` (never estimated).
ModelSpeed.title: ModelSpeed

ModelUse.description: One model of a release and where it is used.
ModelUse.title: ModelUse

NativeToolSupport.description: A provider-native tool (run by the provider, never by Nodestro) and whether this model can use it.
NativeToolSupport.title: NativeToolSupport

NeededRequirement.description: A direct requirement of a scope: the union of what its tools need.
NeededRequirement.title: NeededRequirement

NetworkNeed.description: Something the release needs a network connection or an outside service for.
NetworkNeed.title: NetworkNeed

OptionSupport.description:
Whether an agent option can be used with a model; ``reason`` says why not (a code the editor translates).

Reasons: ``provider`` (the provider's API has no such setting), ``model`` (the model does not accept it),
``automatic`` (the provider does it by itself, e.g. prompt caching at OpenAI and Gemini), ``not_mapped`` (the
provider has a similar feature that Nodestro does not offer as this option), ``unknown`` (not documented for this
model).
OptionSupport.title: OptionSupport

OrchestratorConfig.description:
An AI model that delegates the task to teams of its pool until it can answer (AO M4).

It only selects: it creates no agents and no tools, and has no tools of its own. Each chosen team
runs as a linked child run with its own budget, limits and tool approvals; the orchestrator's
decisions, reasons and the teams' results are recorded (``NodeRun.orchestration``).
OrchestratorConfig.title: OrchestratorConfig

OrchestratorMember.description: A team in an orchestrator's pool: a saved workflow, run as a sub-workflow when chosen.
OrchestratorMember.title: OrchestratorMember

OrchestratorSelect.description:
Pool selection by capability (AO M5): saved workflows whose capabilities match join the pool.

The selection is made when a run (or a published release) pins its workflows, so it is fixed and
visible in the run's snapshot: every selected member names the tags it matched. Teams are ordered
by the number of matching tags, then by name; no score is invented. Workflows with errors and the
workflow itself are left out. Teams with approval steps are offered: the orchestrator waits while
one of them waits for a person (AO M6b).
OrchestratorSelect.title: OrchestratorSelect

OutputConfig.description: Plain text, or a structured result described by fields (a Pydantic model is built from them).
OutputConfig.title: OutputConfig

OverrideIn.description: An individual price (USD per million tokens, as decimal strings): a contract price or a correction.
OverrideIn.title: OverrideIn

Plan.description: The approval overview: what would be installed, nothing has happened yet.
Plan.title: Plan

requirement.description: Precise specification: purpose, inputs with types and units, output, edge cases.
requirement.title: Requirement

PortableCheck.description: What a portable package of the release would contain and need (:mod:`nodestro_api.portable_build`).
PortableCheck.title: PortableCheck

PriceChange.description: One difference between the active reference prices and a candidate.
PriceChange.title: PriceChange

PriceEntry.description: The effective price of one model, with everything a user needs to judge it.
PriceEntry.title: PriceEntry

PriceIssue.description: A finding of :func:`validate_snapshot`. ``error`` drops the price; ``warning`` keeps it.
PriceIssue.title: PriceIssue

PricingEvent.description: One entry of the price history (``price_events``).
PricingEvent.title: PricingEvent

PricingOverview.description: The catalog's state plus what the studio needs to explain it.
PricingOverview.title: PricingOverview

ProvidedFile.description: A file an agent received, and how (shown in the trace).
ProvidedFile.title: ProvidedFile

ProviderInfo.description: What a provider needs and offers (static; the interface translates it by ``id``).
ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo

ProviderSettingsIn.description:
A change of one provider's settings: ``None`` keeps a value, an empty text removes it.

``region``, ``auth``, ``profile_name`` and ``data_residency`` belong to Amazon Bedrock only (other providers
refuse them with ``provider.field_not_supported``); Bedrock refuses ``api_key``, ``base_url`` and
``capabilities``.
ProviderSettingsIn.title: ProviderSettingsIn

ProviderStatus.description: A provider as the settings page shows it; never contains the key itself.
ProviderStatus.title: ProviderStatus

ProviderVerification.description: The result of the last explicit check of a provider (Bedrock); never an account, ARN or key.
ProviderVerification.title: ProviderVerification

ProviderVerifyIn.description:
What to check: without ``model`` the region's model list is read; with one, that model or inference profile
(``eu.anthropic...``, an ARN; ``bedrock:`` in front is accepted).
ProviderVerifyIn.title: ProviderVerifyIn

PublicationBudget.description: The daily cost limit of one published API and how much of it the last 24 hours used (AD-20).
PublicationBudget.title: PublicationBudget

PublicationOverviewItem.description:
One publication on the studio's *Publications* page: the stored publication, its workflow, the active
release and the export history. Read only; everything comes from the stored publications, releases and
export records (nothing is stored for the page).
PublicationOverviewItem.title: PublicationOverviewItem

PublishedError.description: Every error answer of a published API (``{"error": {...}}``; see :class:`ApiError`).
PublishedError.title: PublishedError

PublishedErrorDetail.description: The error of a published API's answer: HTTP status, a stable code, an English message and parameters.
PublishedErrorDetail.title: PublishedErrorDetail

PythonEnvironment.description: The stored definition of one scope's environment.
PythonEnvironment.title: PythonEnvironment

PythonLock.description: Approved third-party libraries of one workflow's tools (``uv pip compile`` output).
PythonLock.title: PythonLock

QualityConfig.description: An LLM judge that checks the result and lets the agent revise it (``orkexa.refine``).
QualityConfig.title: QualityConfig

Readiness.description: The answer of a readiness check: ``problem`` is ``None`` when the model can be used now.
Readiness.title: Readiness

ReasoningStreamInfo.description: What a model's stream transmits of its reasoning, for the interface (``orkexa.ReasoningStream``).
ReasoningStreamInfo.title: ReasoningStreamInfo

ReasoningTrace.description: The reasoning of one model call sequence as it arrived (a run step, an agent test, a chat answer).
ReasoningTrace.title: ReasoningTrace

Recommendation.description: The model suggested for a task, and why.
Recommendation.title: Recommendation

ReferenceUser.description: One place that uses the object.
ReferenceUser.title: ReferenceUser

ReleaseGate.description: What a new release of a publication must show (opt-in per publication).
ReleaseGate.title: ReleaseGate

assumptions.description: Reasonable assumptions for details the description leaves open (short sentences).
assumptions.title: Assumptions

goal.description: One or two sentences: what the workflow achieves for the user.
goal.title: Goal

inputs.description: What the user provides when starting a run.
inputs.title: Inputs

question.description: Only if an essential detail is missing so that no sensible workflow can be designed: one precise question. Otherwise null.
question.title: Question

title.description: A short name for the workflow, at most 60 characters.
title.title: Title

ResultFileSpec.description: A file the result node writes at the end of a run (see :mod:`nodestro_runtime.reports`).
ResultFileSpec.title: ResultFileSpec

ReviewOut.description: A snapshot held back because some of its changes need a person's decision.
ReviewOut.title: ReviewOut

RunBudget.description:
The budget of one run, apart from every configuration it came from (BUDGET-1).

``initial_limit_usd`` is the effective limit the run started with (the workflow's budget, else the workspace's
default budget, or a published release's run limit); ``limit_usd`` is the limit that applies now: the initial one
or the last approved raise. A raise changes only this run: never the workflow, its saved versions or the
settings, and never another run. ``None`` limits mean: no limit.
RunBudget.title: RunBudget

RunCause.title: RunCause

RunMessage.description: One message of a run's live chat.
RunMessage.title: RunMessage

RunWarning.description:
Something a run that ended went without (AD-03): e.g. a tool call that was refused, timed out or failed.

``code`` is the call's problem code (``tool.approval_rejected``, ``tool.approval_timeout``, ``tool.not_granted``,
``mcp.unreachable``, ...; ``tool.failed`` when the tool's error has no code); ``count`` calls of ``tool`` in
``node_id`` had it.
RunWarning.title: RunWarning

SampleInfo.description: A sample file as the gallery lists it (download: ``/api/library/{id}/samples/{sample}``).
SampleInfo.title: SampleInfo

SandboxBackendStatus.description: One sandbox backend of the computer the runtime runs on, as the policy sees it.
SandboxBackendStatus.title: SandboxBackendStatus

SandboxCheck.description: One check behind a backend's state, e.g. ``preflight`` or ``self-test`` of the Docker sandbox.
SandboxCheck.title: SandboxCheck

SandboxSelection.description: Where tool code runs now on the computer the runtime runs on (not the browser's).
SandboxSelection.title: SandboxSelection

SandboxStatus.description: The Docker row of the settings' ``sandbox_backends``, and what this request did about it.
SandboxStatus.title: SandboxStatus

SanitizeReport.description: What a sanitized trace export removed; travels in the exported file as ``sanitized``.
SanitizeReport.title: SanitizeReport

SecretIn.description: The new secret; ``""`` removes it. Never returned by any route.
SecretIn.title: SecretIn

SentFile.description: A file a message was sent with, and how the model received it.
SentFile.title: SentFile

ServerToolInfo.description: A tool run by the provider itself; these are Anthropic's server tools.
ServerToolInfo.title: ServerToolInfo

SettingsDefaults.description:
The value each setting of ``GET /api/settings`` has while nobody changed it (API-061), so an interface can mark
a field as "default" or "changed". The defaults of the output limits are ``output_limit_defaults`` of the
settings; provider settings have no default.
SettingsDefaults.title: SettingsDefaults

Snapshot.description: What the assistant gets of one object at one point in time; never changed afterwards.
Snapshot.title: Snapshot

StdioCommand.description:
A local MCP server started over stdio (WP-8): Python packages from PyPI, installed only after an administrator
approved their hash-pinned versions, and run with ``python -m <module> <args>`` in a container of Nodestro's
sandbox image: no network, read-only root file system, no capabilities, user ``nobody``, memory/CPU/process
limits. Never on the host.
StdioCommand.title: StdioCommand

Step.description: Something the assistant actually did while answering.
Step.title: Step

SubworkflowConfig.description: Another saved workflow, run as one step of this one (same engine, own child run).
SubworkflowConfig.title: SubworkflowConfig

TeamActivity.description: One team an orchestrator gave work to, as stored now.
TeamActivity.title: TeamActivity

TemplateTeam.description: A team an orchestrator of the template can delegate to (a part, copied as a workflow of its own).
TemplateTeam.title: TemplateTeam

ToolAdoption.description: A person's confirmed adoption of one version of an AI-generated tool as their own code (ADR-0006, R-4).
ToolAdoption.title: ToolAdoption

ToolApprovalEvent.description:
One entry of a tenant's approval audit trail: who decided, granted or revoked what, when; and every refused
decision with its problem code. Never holds the call's arguments (only their hash).
ToolApprovalEvent.title: ToolApprovalEvent

ToolBinding.description:
When an agent asks before calling one of its tools.

- ``auto`` (every new binding): ask when the tool does more than read.
- ``always``: ask for every call.
- ``never``: do not ask. Counts only for ``read`` tools, for ``write`` tools with a ``reason`` and for legacy
  exemptions; never for ``destructive`` tools. Otherwise it is treated as ``auto``.

A **legacy exemption** (``legacy``) is a binding that existed before S-2; it holds only for the tool version it
was bound to (``bound_version``): a new version of the tool ends it.
ToolBinding.title: ToolBinding

ToolCallApproval.description: What the per-call approval rules did with one call.
ToolCallApproval.title: ToolCallApproval

ToolCapability.description: What a tool may do (see the module documentation).
ToolCapability.title: ToolCapability

ToolDefinition.description: What a server says about a tool: the part whose hash pins an approval.
ToolDefinition.title: ToolDefinition

ToolIssue.description: A dependency problem of one tool (an unknown module, a dynamic import, ...).
ToolIssue.title: ToolIssue

message.default: The Coding Agent is writing code and tests
message.title: Message

ToolPreGrant.description:
A person's advance approval of one tool for one unattended scope (D10c): narrow, traceable, revocable.

Matches only the tool name, its version (own and generated tools) and the scope; voided by a new tool version,
by its expiry and by revocation. Never covers ``destructive`` or MCP tools.
ToolPreGrant.title: ToolPreGrant

ToolSettings.description:
How an agent binds one built-in tool (NAL-A1, ADR-0001): the service connection it uses and its binding
parameters (validated against the tool's ``params_schema``). Never visible to the model.
ToolSettings.title: ToolSettings

ToolSpec.description: The catalog entry of one built-in tool (see the module documentation).
ToolSpec.title: ToolSpec

UnreconciledProvider.description: A provider Nodestro estimated costs for in the period but did not compare with a bill.
UnreconciledProvider.title: UnreconciledProvider

UploadResult.description: One uploaded file: stored (``file``) or refused (``problem``).
UploadResult.title: UploadResult

UsageBudgets.description: Budgets in the usage report (AD-20): the daily limits of published APIs and the runs budgets stopped.
UsageBudgets.title: UsageBudgets

ValueWarning.description:
A key figure (``source="tool"``) that the agent's own computing tool calls in the test do not back (RT-054).

A workflow run would ask the agent once to correct it and then fail the step (``run.value_unverified``); the
test only warns, because a step that copies a figure an earlier step computed has no earlier steps here.
``reason`` as :class:`~nodestro_runtime.value_checks.Unverified`: ``missing``, ``not_from_tool``,
``table_incomplete`` or ``table_changed``.
ValueWarning.title: ValueWarning

WorkflowLimits.description: Execution limits of a workflow's runs (Adaptive Orchestration M2); ``None``: no limit of this kind.
WorkflowLimits.title: WorkflowLimits

WorkflowOrigin.description:
Where a workflow came from when it was made as a copy (RT-055): today a copy of an example.

Set once by the code that makes the copy and kept by every later save (:func:`keep_origin`): it is history, not
something an editor or a client sends (``WorkflowIn`` has no such field). An interface uses it to mark a copy
whose integrations run on sample data, or to offer the example's newer version.
WorkflowOrigin.title: WorkflowOrigin

WorkflowSummary.description: A workflow in the list; ``contract`` keeps the field names, ``contract_fields`` describes them (API-053).
WorkflowSummary.title: WorkflowSummary

nodestro_runtime__release__KnowledgeRef.description: A knowledge file an agent uses: referenced live data, not part of the version.
nodestro_runtime__release__KnowledgeRef.title: KnowledgeRef

get.description:
The access audit trail of this workspace (on a server: of the tenant), newest first (API-004): logins and
refused logins, tenant switches and logouts, API key changes, and the operator's tenant and member commands.
Read only; it never holds a secret.

schema.title: Response Access Audit Events Api Access Audit Get
Response List Templates Api Agents Templates Get

post.description:

The result is returned, never stored as a run; its usage goes to the ledger. Testing costs money (``run``); a

post.description:
Approve or reject one tool call; the waiting run continues at its next look (within about a second). A run
paused at the call (agent checkpoints, M6b) continues right away once none of its calls waits any more.

Run the Docker sandbox's checks again now, the in-container self-test included, and wait at most
``timeout`` seconds (default 30, at most 60) for the result. A check that takes longer (the first start builds
the runtime image) goes on in the background: the answer then says ``checking`` and ``GET
/api/sandbox/status`` shows the result later. Within 10 s of the last self-test no new one starts: the answer is
the status of the running or last check with ``throttled`` and ``retry_after`` (``check_started`` false).
Readers cannot start checks, and ``refresh`` on the status has a window of its own, so neither delays this.

get.description:
The Docker sandbox of the computer the API runs on, as the background check last found it (the ``docker``
row of the settings' ``sandbox_backends``). It never waits for the daemon: ``state`` is ``checking`` until the
first check after the start finished, and ``approved`` only after the preflight and the in-container self-test
passed (``checks`` lists each step).

``refresh=1`` starts a new check in the background, the self-test included, and answers at once with the
current status; only administrators start one (otherwise ``refresh_ignored``), at most every 10 s (otherwise
``throttled`` with ``retry_after``); ``check_started`` says whether this request started one. ``wait`` (seconds,
at most 5) waits that long at most for a running check, unless too many requests wait already
(``wait_skipped``). Without ``admin`` host details are left out (``redacted``).
